gaps.sentence: It took a great ___ of courage to admit the mistake.
gaps.explanation: 'A great deal of courage' is the standard pattern with uncountables; 'a great number of' needs countables.

gaps.sentence: She has ___ patience with excuses; deliver on time or do not bother coming.
gaps.explanation: 'Has no patience with' — 'no' directly negates the noun.

gaps.sentence: She spent a great ___ of time preparing the report.
gaps.hint: fixed phrase: a great ___ of + uncountable
gaps.explanation: 'A great deal of time' is used with uncountable nouns; 'a great number of' needs a countable plural.

gaps.sentence: There is ___ use asking him — he never checks his messages.
gaps.explanation: 'There is no use doing something' = it is pointless.

gaps.sentence: ___ of the two proposals has been approved so far.
gaps.explanation: 'Neither of the two' — 'none' is for three or more.

gaps.sentence: If you walk instead of driving, you'll spend ___ on petrol.
gaps.explanation: 'Spend less' is the comparative with uncountable money; 'fewer' is for countable nouns.
'Far too much information' is the correct intensifier pattern; 'far much' and 'far very' do not exist.

gaps.sentence: ___ students joined the trip this year than last.
